children: Happiest Minds Technologies shares plunged more than 8 percent in morning trade on September 1, emerging among the top smallcap losers after the IT services company announced a merger with ITC Infotech alongside a Rs 1,330-crore promoter stake sale.

The stock was trading 8.3 percent lower at Rs 373 in morning trade, extending its year-to-date decline to 18.3 percent. The Nifty 50, in comparison, is down 8.1 percent so far this year. Happiest Minds' market capitalisation stood at Rs 5,682 crore. Meanwhile, ITC Infotech parent ITC Ltd's stock was up about 3 percent.

The decline came after Happiest Minds founder and executive chairman Ashok Soota and Ashok Soota Medical Research LLP agreed to sell a 22.1 percent stake in the company to ITC Infotech for Rs 1,329.72 crore. The acquisition will be followed by the merger of Happiest Minds into ITC Infotech, subject to statutory and regulatory approvals.

The promoter stake sale will take place in two tranches. ITC Infotech will first acquire an 11 percent stake at Rs 390 per share for Rs 653.26 crore, followed by another 11.106 percent stake at Rs 400 per share for Rs 676.46 crore.

The first-tranche acquisition price of Rs 390 represents a discount of about 4.2 percent to Happiest Minds' previous closing price of Rs 406.95, while the second-tranche price of Rs 400 is about 1.7 percent lower.

Under the proposed merger, Happiest Minds shareholders will receive 25 fully paid-up shares of ITC Infotech for every 81 shares they hold. The combined entity will subsequently be listed on the BSE and NSE, while Happiest Minds will be dissolved without being wound up once the scheme becomes effective.

Happiest Minds said on CNBC-TV18 that it is valued at 15.1 times EBITDA under the transaction, compared with 13.6 times for ITC Infotech. ITC Infotech is about 2.17 times larger in terms of revenue and profit and also has a higher cash balance.
ITC will own approximately 74 percent of the combined company after the integration. Happiest Minds also said there will be no open offer under the current transaction structure.
The companies are targeting revenue of more than $1 billion by FY28 for the combined entity. On a pro-forma basis, the merged business had an operating margin of around 18-18.3 percent.

Happiest Minds said detailed integration discussions have not yet taken place, but there is no meaningful overlap among the top customers of the two companies. The merger is expected to improve the combined entity's ability to compete with larger IT services companies.
